998	## HermiteWord
   999	
  1000	Checks the combinatorial core of `L:finite-word-cutoff` (exact cutoffs for
  1001	finite Gaussian words), which is applied in `P:static-phase-all-orders` and
  1002	`L:fixed-split`: if the initial vector has degree zero in every color, each
  1003	step raises a degree bound by one in its color and
  1004	the projection fixes every vector within the cutoff, inserting the
  1005	projection around each step does not change the word. The statements are
  1006	abstract (arbitrary types and maps). The companion file
  1007	`HermiteWordConsumer.lean` instantiates them with the scalar Hermite
  1008	recurrence `x He_n = He_(n+1) + n He_(n-1)` as private worked examples; it
  1009	adds no public declarations. The Hermite/Fock realization is proved in
  1010	`FockForm` (`goodDeg_vac`, `goodDeg_insert`, `goodDeg_frame`, `truncC_eq`, one
  1011	Gaussian coordinate per color) and applied in
  1012	`HermiteWordFock.cut_eq_raw_fock` (next section).

2663	## GaussianHermite (whole result)
  2664	
  2665	A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and
  2666	nothing is supplied. The manuscript (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  2667	at `a284420`, main TeX) uses "normalized Hermite polynomials" in three
  2668	proofs: `L:fock-form` (lines 2515-2517), the multiplication bound
  2669	`E:occupied-multiplication` inside the proof of `P:mild-construction`
  2670	(lines 1805-1810) and `L:finite-word-cutoff` (lines 2556-2558). It uses
  2671	two facts about them: multiplication by the coordinate `g_i` acts by
  2672	`g_i h_k = sqrt(k_i+1) h_(k+e_i) + sqrt(k_i) h_(k-e_i)`, and the `h_k`
  2673	are orthonormal under independent standard Gaussians. The TeX takes the
  2674	creation and annihilation algebra from Janson (cited at lines 2467-2468).
  2675	This module proves both facts, and the spanning step of
  2676	`E:occupied-multiplication`.
  2677	
  2678	Formalized. The probabilists' Hermite polynomials `He_n` are Mathlib's
  2679	`Polynomial.hermite` mapped to real coefficients (`hermR`, values `He`).
  2680	The module proves the Appell property `He_(n+1)' = (n+1) He_n` (absent from
  2681	Mathlib), the recurrences, Gaussian integration by parts on polynomials
  2682	(`gE_X_mul`, from `GaussianIBP.integral_mul_eq_integral_deriv`), the shift
  2683	`E[He_(n+1) q] = E[He_n q']`, and orthogonality
  2684	`E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm)`. The normalized `h_n = He_n/sqrt(n!)` are
  2685	orthonormal (`integral_hn_mul_hn`) and satisfy
  2686	`x h_n = sqrt(n+1) h_(n+1) + sqrt(n) h_(n-1)` (`mul_hn`). The products
  2687	`h_k(x) = prod_i h_(k_i)(x_i)` on `R^m` are orthonormal under
  2688	`GaussianIBP.stdPi m`, the product of `m` standard Gaussian laws
  2689	(`integral_hk_mul_hk`), and satisfy the coordinate recurrence of the TeX
  2690	(`coord_mul_hk`). The spanning step: every real polynomial in
  2691	`x_1, ..., x_m` of total degree at most `n` is a real combination of the
  2692	`h_l` with `|l| <= n` (`mvPolynomial_mem_hermiteSpan`, via
  2693	`monomial_mem_hermiteSpan` and the triangularity `pow_mem_span1`).
  2694	
  2695	Abstractions. Gaussian coordinates are the coordinate functions on
  2696	`Fin m -> R` under `stdPi m`; the transfer to independent standard Gaussians
  2697	on a probability space is `GaussianIBP.integral_comp_eq_stdPi`, used in
  2698	`FockForm.occupied_multiplication_paper`. Multi-indices are functions
  2699	`Fin m -> N`; `k - e_i` is pointwise truncated subtraction.
  2700	
  2701	Junk values. None of the statements depends on one: `sqrt(n!) > 0`, every
  2702	integral statement comes with its integrability, and `k - e_i` (or `n - 1`)
  2703	only appears multiplied by a coefficient that vanishes exactly when the
  2704	subtraction truncates: `sqrt(k_i)` (or `sqrt(n)`) in the normalized
  2705	formulas, `k_i` (or `n`, as in `n * hermR (n - 1)`) in the unnormalized ones.
  2706	
  2707	Not formalized here: the closed Gaussian polynomial spaces, infinitely many
  2708	coordinates, and the Wiener chaos decomposition. Labelling: a row is
  2709	labelled with a manuscript step only where the TeX states it (the
  2710	recurrence and the orthonormality of the normalized polynomials, and the
  2711	spanning step of `E:occupied-multiplication`, which the TeX uses when it
  2712	passes to "finite-coordinate polynomials"); the remaining public facts are
  2713	foundation rows ("no direct label") or route helpers.
  2714	
  2715	Refutations (`refutations/gaussian-hermite/`, each a Lean proof that a
  2716	wrong variant is false, with the package statement at the same point):
  2717	`OrthogonalityNoDelta` (dropping the Kronecker delta in
  2718	`E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm)`), `UnnormalizedOrthonormal` (`E[He_2^2] = 2`,
  2719	so the normalization is needed) and `RecurrenceNoLowering` (dropping the
  2720	lowering term of `mul_hn`).

  2928	## HermiteFock (whole result)
  2929	
  2930	A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and
  2931	nothing is supplied. It is the finite Gaussian Fock layer used in
  2932	`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420` (main TeX):
  2933	the Fock half of the proof of `L:fock-form` (lines 2515-2526), the Fock
  2934	sentences of the proof of `L:interval-contractions` (lines 2887-2891), the
  2935	phase insertion on a color in its vacuum (lines 2838-2841 and 2878-2880),
  2936	and the Hermite step of `E:occupied-multiplication` (lines 1805-1810). The
  2937	TeX cites Janson (lines 2467-2468) for the creation and annihilation
  2938	algebra; this module proves what is used.
  2939	
  2940	Model (decision 5 of wave L9). The Gaussian `L^2` space with values in a
  2941	complex inner product space `X` is represented by coefficient vectors
  2942	`(Fin m -> N) -> X`, indexed by multi-indices, restricted to total degree
  2943	at most `N` (`degLE m N`; `Supp N v` says `v` vanishes above degree `N`).
  2944	The expansion `iota N v (x) = sum_(|k| <= N) h_k(x) v_k` in the normalized
  2945	Hermite functions of `GaussianHermite` links the two pictures: it is an
  2946	isometry into `L^2(stdPi m; X)` (`integral_norm_sq_iota`; `stdPi m` is the
  2947	law of `m` independent standard Gaussians), multiplication by `x_i` is
  2948	`a_i^* + a_i` on coefficients (`coord_smul_iota`), and `sum_i x_i H_i` is
  2949	the field operator `fieldOp H` (`sum_coord_smul_iota`). No tensor-product
  2950	inner product is used: the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is `X` itself,
  2951	and the spatial operators `H_i` are continuous linear maps of `X`. The TeX
  2952	rotates `H/||H||` to a first coordinate (line 1805); the general column
  2953	form with operators `H_i` makes that step unnecessary. Convention: Mathlib's
  2954	inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, whereas the TeX's is
  2955	linear in the first slot (line 2824); every adjoint identity stated here
  2956	survives the conjugation, and the norm-square and real-part identities are
  2957	unchanged.
  2958	
  2959	Formalized. The annihilation and creation operators
  2960	`(a_i v)_k = sqrt(k_i+1) v_(k+e_i)`, `(a_i^* v)_k = sqrt(k_i) v_(k-e_i)`,
  2961	the number identity `sum_i a_i^* a_i = |k|`, and the finite adjoint
  2962	identity between `a_i` and `a_i^*`. The creation row from degrees `<= N` to
  2963	degrees `<= N+1` has norm at most `sqrt(N+1)` (`creRow_bound`), attained on
  2964	`u_i = a_i w` for `w` of exact degree `N+1` (`creRow_attained`). For
  2965	symmetric `H_1, ..., H_m` with the column bound
  2966	`sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2`, `c >= 0` (hypotheses of these lemmas, not
  2967	manuscript inputs here), the field operator `sum_i (a_i^* + a_i) (x) H_i`
  2968	maps degrees `<= N` to degrees `<= N+1` with norm at most
  2969	`2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(c)` (`fieldOp_bound`), the same after truncation to
  2970	degrees `<= N` (`fieldOp_bound_trunc`), the truncated operator is symmetric
  2971	(`fieldOp_symm_trunc`), and both bounds hold in Gaussian `L^2` with
  2972	integrability (`gaussian_field_bound`, `gaussian_field_bound_trunc`).
  2973	Vacuum insertion: `E||sum_i g_i w_i||^2 = sum_i ||w_i||^2`
  2974	(`vacuum_insertion_isometry`).
  2975	
  2976	Route difference. The TeX bounds the annihilation part as the adjoint of
  2977	the creation part (line 2522); Lean uses the same adjoint relation through
  2978	the finite identity `sum_inner_ann` and Cauchy-Schwarz. Its annihilation
  2979	theorem maps input degrees `<= N+1` to output degrees `<= N` with squared
  2980	norm at most `(N+1) c`; the TeX's `sqrt(n)` (lines 1806-1809) concerns input
  2981	degrees `<= n`, so the two operator domains are indexed differently, and the
  2982	Fock proof says "the same bound after truncation" (lines 2522-2523). Applied
  2983	to an input already supported through `N`, the `N+1`-to-`N` theorem leaves
  2984	an unused degree of slack. The constant `4(N+1)c` of the sum does not need
  2985	the sharper value.
  2986	
  2987	Junk values. The truncated subtraction `k - e_i` occurs only multiplied by
  2988	`sqrt(k_i)`, which vanishes exactly when it truncates; `c >= 0` is a
  2989	hypothesis where it is used; every integral conclusion includes
  2990	integrability. Coefficient vectors are arbitrary functions; only their
  2991	values in degrees `<= N` (or `<= N+1`) enter the stated sums.
  2992	
  2993	Not formalized here: the full Gaussian `L^2` space, infinitely many
  2994	coordinates, the closed polynomial spaces and unbounded number operators.
  2995	
  2996	Refutations (`refutations/hermite-fock/`): `CreRowConstant` (the constant
  2997	`N` in place of `N+1` in `creRow_bound` fails at the vacuum), `NumberOrder`
  2998	(`|k| + 1` in place of `|k|` in `number_identity`) and `VacuumSquareOfSum`
  2999	(`(sum_i ||w_i||)^2` in place of `sum_i ||w_i||^2` in
  3000	`vacuum_insertion_isometry`).

3190	## IntervalScalar (whole result)
  3191	
  3192	Formalizes the deterministic scalar, combinatorial and Hilbert-space steps of
  3193	two results of `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`:
  3194	`C:static-interaction` (statement lines 2685-2731, proof 2733-2796) and
  3195	`P:interval-coefficients` (statement lines 3402-3414, proof 3416-3581). Both
  3196	results are operator and stochastic statements; every row below is a step row
  3197	(class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement), except
  3198	`E:static-block-series`, which is a scalar statement and is proved in full with
  3199	nothing supplied (`static_block_series_paper`). The operator and stochastic
  3200	inputs enter as named hypotheses; the last column names each one with its
  3201	manuscript label.
  3202	
  3203	`C:static-interaction`. `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)` is modelled by an arbitrary
  3204	complete real inner product space `E`, and the transported phases
  3205	`Y_n = S_0(-h) Z_n^eps(h)` by a sequence `Y : N -> E`; the expectation of an
  3206	inner product is the inner product of `E`. This is faithful because the proof
  3207	of `E:static-interaction` (lines 2733-2770) uses only the Hilbert structure:
  3208	the order bounds of lines 2746-2751, the Gaussian parity of line 2752, and
  3209	the two first-variance bounds of lines 2737-2742. Those are the supplied
  3210	hypotheses `hY0`, `hY`, `hodd`, `hborn`, `hmean`. The identification of
  3211	`I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g)` with `sum sigma^n Y_n` (lines 2687-2692) is not
  3212	formalized. Lean proves that `sum sigma^n Y_n` converges and the bound
  3213	`(1 + E(h, sigma, lambda)) N^2`. `L_alpha`, `B_alpha`, `x` and `E` are the
  3214	definitions `staticL`, `staticB`, `staticX`, `staticE`, word for word; `A`
  3215	stands for `A_alpha` and may be any constant `>= 0`. The section's constants
  3216	are `R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` and `D_Gamma` of
  3217	`E:phase-constants` (lines 2058-2065), for locally finite `mu`, `Gamma` on
  3218	`R^3` and `0 < alpha < 2`. These are the only clauses of the TeX's covariance
  3219	class (line 2054) in the wrappers. Evenness, positive definiteness and scaling
  3220	enter only through the supplied hypotheses. `R_alpha >= 0` and `D_Gamma >= 0`
  3221	are derived (`ralpha_nonneg`, `dgamma_nonneg`). The `_step` and
  3222	`static_block_series` forms take them as hypotheses. The TeX argues with the
  3223	absolutely convergent double series; Lean bounds the partial sums, regrouped
  3224	by `r + s = 2k` (`square_sum_eq`), keeps the first coefficient signed, and
  3225	passes to the limit. For `E:independent-static-blocks`, Lean proves the scalar
  3226	iteration and `1 + y <= e^y`. The per-block bound
  3227	`m_(j+1) <= e^(lambda h_j)(1 + E) m_j` is supplied (lines 2787-2793: it uses
  3228	`E:static-interaction`, `\|S_0(h_j)\|^2 <= e^(lambda h_j)`, density and
  3229	tensoring with the independent past). The operators `M_j(h_j)` and their
  3230	`L^2` extensions are not formalized. Hypotheses carried but unused: `0 < alpha`
  3231	in `static_interaction_step`; `0 < alpha` in `static_block_series` (its
  3232	`0 < alpha0` is used: with `alpha + alpha0 < 2` it gives `alpha < 2`); local finiteness of `mu`, `Gamma` (it only makes the
  3233	ball masses finite, so that `toReal` is not a junk value); `lambda h_j <= 1` in
  3234	`independent_static_blocks_paper`.
  3235	
  3236	`P:interval-coefficients`. The energy coefficient `[s^(2k)] E\|U(T;s)v\|^2`,
  3237	the split inner products `Q_(r,q)` and `\|v\|_(1/T)^2` are real numbers `coef`,
  3238	`Q p`, `V`. Colors are `j : Fin M` with the TeX's sorted label `i = j + 1`.
  3239	Supplied hypotheses:
  3240	- `hsplits`: `E:interval-energy-splits` combined with the reflection parity
  3241	  (lines 3478-3488).
  3242	- `hfixed`: `L:fixed-split` (`E:fixed-split-bound`; lemma lines 3053-3094) at
  3243	  `lambda = k/T`. Its per-color factor is `splitFactor`, with `l_i` as
  3244	  `splitEll`.

  3265	  3549-3566). For `E:interval-phase-bound` (lines 3567-3579), Lean proves

  3267	  R_alpha^(1/nu) T^(beta/nu)) V`, the TeX's display with its absorbed constant
  3268	  `nu C^(1/nu)`, from four supplied hypotheses:
  3269	- the power-series identity at `s = 1`;
  3270	- vanishing odd coefficients;
  3271	- the zero-order bound `e V`;
  3272	- the coefficient bound.

  3274	(`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, line 225; the section's standing
  3275	class at lines 2814-2819 is that of `H:homog`), from which `0 < alpha < 2`,

  3279	Junk values: in the manuscript-facing bounds every real power has a positive
  3280	base, or is `(k!)^nu`, or is `i^q` with `i >= 1` (or a nonnegative base with a

     1	# Stratonovich HAM second moment: Lean companion
     2	
     3	Lean 4 checks of finite, algebraic and scalar steps in the paper
     4	
     5	> Le Chen, *The second moment of the hyperbolic Anderson model* (in
     6	> preparation).
     7	
     8	The paper studies the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with temporal
     9	covariance `|s-t|^(-α₀)` and homogeneous spatial covariance of order `α`.
    10	It shows that `log E[u(t,x)²]` grows on the scale `t^κ`, with
    11	`κ = (4-α-α₀)/(3-α)`, and identifies the limit by a variational formula.
    12	
    13	**This is a partial formalization.** Lean checks the steps listed below. It
    14	does not check the paper end to end. The SPDE, its solution, the
    15	Stratonovich integrals, the Gaussian noise and the analytic estimates are
    16	outside Lean. Where a checked step needs such a fact, the Lean statement takes
    17	it as an explicit hypothesis, and the paper's proof supplies it.
    18

    13	`g_i` acts by `g_i h_k = √(k_i+1) h_{k+e_i} + √(k_i) h_{k-e_i}`, and the

    21	  The Appell property `He_{n+1}' = (n+1) He_n` (`derivative_hermR_succ`; absent
    22	  from Mathlib) and the three-term recurrence
    23	  `He_{n+2} = x He_{n+1} - (n+1) He_n` (`hermR_succ_succ`).
    24	* `gE p = ∫ p dN(0,1)` for a real polynomial `p`; every polynomial is

    64	/-! ### One variable: the polynomials -/
    65	
    66	/-- The probabilists' Hermite polynomial `He_n` (Mathlib's `Polynomial.hermite`)
    67	with real coefficients. -/
    68	def hermR (n : ℕ) : ℝ[X] := (hermite n).map (Int.castRingHom ℝ)
    69	
    70	/-- The value `He_n(x)`. -/
    71	def He (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := (hermR n).eval x
    72	
    73	/-- Auxiliary (absent from Mathlib): the Appell property over `ℤ`,
    74	`He_{n+1}' = (n+1) He_n`. -/
    75	theorem derivative_hermite_succ : ∀ n : ℕ,
    76	    derivative (hermite (n + 1)) = ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ[X]) * hermite n
    77	  | 0 => by simp [hermite_zero]
    78	  | n + 1 => by
    79	    have ih := derivative_hermite_succ n
    80	    rw [hermite_succ (n + 1), derivative_sub, derivative_mul, derivative_X, ih,
    81	      derivative_mul, derivative_natCast, zero_mul, zero_add]
    82	    rw [hermite_succ n]; push_cast; ring
    83	
    84	/-- `He_0 = 1`. -/
    85	theorem hermR_zero : hermR 0 = 1 := by simp [hermR]
    86	
    87	/-- `He_{n+1} = x He_n - He_n'`. -/
    88	theorem hermR_succ (n : ℕ) : hermR (n + 1) = X * hermR n - derivative (hermR n) := by
    89	  simp only [hermR, hermite_succ, Polynomial.map_sub, Polynomial.map_mul, Polynomial.map_X,
    90	    derivative_map]
    91	
    92	/-- The Appell property `He_{n+1}' = (n+1) He_n`. -/
    93	theorem derivative_hermR_succ (n : ℕ) :
    94	    derivative (hermR (n + 1)) = ((n : ℝ[X]) + 1) * hermR n := by
    95	  simp only [hermR, derivative_map, derivative_hermite_succ, Polynomial.map_mul,
    96	    Polynomial.map_natCast]
    97	  push_cast; ring
    98	
    99	/-- The three-term recurrence `He_{n+2} = x He_{n+1} - (n+1) He_n`. -/
   100	theorem hermR_succ_succ (n : ℕ) :
   101	    hermR (n + 2) = X * hermR (n + 1) - ((n : ℝ[X]) + 1) * hermR n := by
   102	  rw [hermR_succ (n + 1), derivative_hermR_succ]
   103	
   104	/-- `He_n` is monic. -/
   105	theorem hermR_monic (n : ℕ) : (hermR n).Monic := (hermite_monic n).map _
   106	
   107	/-- `He_n` has degree `n`. -/
   108	theorem natDegree_hermR (n : ℕ) : (hermR n).natDegree = n := by
   109	  rw [hermR, (hermite_monic n).natDegree_map, natDegree_hermite]
   110	
   111	/-- Auxiliary: `He_n^{(n)} = n!` as a constant polynomial. -/
   112	theorem iterate_derivative_hermR_self (n : ℕ) :
   113	    derivative^[n] (hermR n) = C (n ! : ℝ) := by
   114	  have hdeg : (derivative^[n] (hermR n)).natDegree ≤ 0 := by
   115	    have := natDegree_iterate_derivative (hermR n) n
   116	    rw [natDegree_hermR] at this; omega
   117	  have hc : (hermR n).coeff n = 1 := by
   118	    have := (hermR_monic n).coeff_natDegree; rwa [natDegree_hermR] at this
   119	  rw [eq_C_of_natDegree_le_zero hdeg, coeff_iterate_derivative, zero_add,
   120	    Nat.descFactorial_self, hc]
   121	  simp
   122	
   123	/-- `He_n' = n He_{n-1}` (for `n = 0` both sides are `0`). -/
   124	theorem derivative_hermR (n : ℕ) :
   125	    derivative (hermR n) = (n : ℝ[X]) * hermR (n - 1) := by
   126	  cases n with
   127	  | zero => simp [hermR_zero]
   128	  | succ n => rw [derivative_hermR_succ]; simp

   130	/-- `x He_n = He_{n+1} + n He_{n-1}`. -/
   131	theorem X_mul_hermR (n : ℕ) :
   132	    X * hermR n = hermR (n + 1) + (n : ℝ[X]) * hermR (n - 1) := by
   133	  rw [hermR_succ, derivative_hermR]; ring

   136	
   137	/-- Every real polynomial is integrable against `N(0,1)`. -/
   138	theorem integrable_eval (p : ℝ[X]) :
   139	    Integrable (fun x => p.eval x) (gaussianReal 0 1) := by
   140	  have h : (fun x => p.eval x) =
   141	      fun x => ∑ i ∈ range (p.natDegree + 1), p.coeff i * x ^ i := by
   142	    funext x; exact eval_eq_sum_range x
   143	  rw [h]
   144	  exact integrable_finsetSum _ fun i _ =>
   145	    (GaussianIBP.integrable_pow_gaussian i).const_mul _
   146	
   147	/-- The Gaussian expectation of a real polynomial. -/
   148	def gE (p : ℝ[X]) : ℝ := ∫ x, p.eval x ∂gaussianReal 0 1
   149	
   150	/-- Auxiliary: additivity of `gE`. -/
   151	theorem gE_add (p q : ℝ[X]) : gE (p + q) = gE p + gE q := by
   152	  simp only [gE, eval_add]; exact integral_add (integrable_eval p) (integrable_eval q)
   153	
   154	/-- Auxiliary: `gE` of a difference. -/
   155	theorem gE_sub (p q : ℝ[X]) : gE (p - q) = gE p - gE q := by
   156	  simp only [gE, eval_sub]; exact integral_sub (integrable_eval p) (integrable_eval q)
   157	
   158	/-- Auxiliary: `gE` of a constant (`N(0,1)` is a probability measure). -/
   159	theorem gE_C (c : ℝ) : gE (C c) = c := by simp [gE]
   160	
   161	/-- Gaussian integration by parts on polynomials: `E[x p] = E[p']`. -/
   162	theorem gE_X_mul (p : ℝ[X]) : gE (X * p) = gE (derivative p) := by
   163	  have h := GaussianIBP.integral_mul_eq_integral_deriv (fun x => p.eval x)
   164	    (fun x => (derivative p).eval x) (fun x => p.hasDerivAt x) (integrable_eval p)
   165	    ((integrable_eval (X * p)).congr (ae_of_all _ fun x => by simp)) (integrable_eval _)
   166	  simpa [gE] using h

   168	/-- The shift `E[He_{n+1} f] = E[He_n f']` for a polynomial `f`. -/
   169	theorem gE_hermR_succ_mul (n : ℕ) (q : ℝ[X]) :
   170	    gE (hermR (n + 1) * q) = gE (hermR n * derivative q) := by
   171	  have h1 : hermR (n + 1) * q = X * (hermR n * q) - derivative (hermR n) * q := by
   172	    rw [hermR_succ]; ring
   173	  have h2 : derivative (hermR n * q) = derivative (hermR n) * q + hermR n * derivative q :=
   174	    derivative_mul
   175	  rw [h1, gE_sub, gE_X_mul, h2, gE_add]; ring

   178	theorem gE_hermR_mul (n : ℕ) (q : ℝ[X]) :

   182	  | succ n ih => rw [gE_hermR_succ_mul, ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
   183	
   184	/-- Polynomial form of the orthogonality: `E[He_n He_m] = n! δ_{nm}`. -/
   185	theorem gE_hermR_mul_hermR (n m : ℕ) :
   186	    gE (hermR n * hermR m) = if n = m then (n ! : ℝ) else 0 := by
   187	  rcases lt_trichotomy n m with h | h | h
   188	  · rw [mul_comm, gE_hermR_mul, iterate_derivative_eq_zero (by rw [natDegree_hermR]; exact h)]
   189	    simpa [h.ne] using gE_C 0
   190	  · subst h; rw [gE_hermR_mul, iterate_derivative_hermR_self, gE_C]; simp
   191	  · rw [gE_hermR_mul, iterate_derivative_eq_zero (by rw [natDegree_hermR]; exact h)]
   192	    simpa [h.ne'] using gE_C 0
   193	
   194	/-- **Orthogonality** `E[He_n(g) He_m(g)] = n! δ_{nm}` for `g ~ N(0,1)`, with
   195	integrability. -/
   196	theorem integral_He_mul_He (n m : ℕ) :
   197	    Integrable (fun x => He n x * He m x) (gaussianReal 0 1) ∧
   198	      ∫ x, He n x * He m x ∂gaussianReal 0 1 = if n = m then (n ! : ℝ) else 0 := by
   199	  refine ⟨by simpa [He] using integrable_eval (hermR n * hermR m), ?_⟩
   200	  rw [← gE_hermR_mul_hermR]; simp [gE, He]
   201	
   202	/-- **The shift** `E[He_{n+1}(g) f(g)] = E[He_n(g) f'(g)]` for a real polynomial
   203	`f`, with integrability of both integrands. -/
   204	theorem integral_He_succ_mul (n : ℕ) (q : ℝ[X]) :
   205	    Integrable (fun x => He (n + 1) x * q.eval x) (gaussianReal 0 1) ∧
   206	      Integrable (fun x => He n x * (derivative q).eval x) (gaussianReal 0 1) ∧
   207	      ∫ x, He (n + 1) x * q.eval x ∂gaussianReal 0 1 =
   208	        ∫ x, He n x * (derivative q).eval x ∂gaussianReal 0 1 := by
   209	  refine ⟨by simpa [He] using integrable_eval (hermR (n + 1) * q),
   210	    by simpa [He] using integrable_eval (hermR n * derivative q), ?_⟩
   211	  have := gE_hermR_succ_mul n q
   212	  simpa [gE, He] using this

   214	/-! ### One variable: normalized Hermite polynomials -/
   215	
   216	/-- The normalized Hermite polynomial `He_n/√(n!)`. -/
   217	def hnPoly (n : ℕ) : ℝ[X] := C (√(n ! : ℝ))⁻¹ * hermR n
   218	
   219	/-- The normalized Hermite function `hn n x = He_n(x)/√(n!)`. -/
   220	def hn (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := (hnPoly n).eval x
   221	
   222	/-- `hn n x = He_n(x)/√(n!)`. -/
   223	theorem hn_eq (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : hn n x = He n x / √(n ! : ℝ) := by
   224	  simp [hn, hnPoly, He, div_eq_inv_mul]
   225	
   226	/-- Auxiliary: `√(n!) > 0`. -/
   227	theorem sqrt_factorial_pos (n : ℕ) : 0 < √(n ! : ℝ) :=
   228	  Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_pos n)
   229	
   230	/-- `hn_0 = 1`. -/
   231	theorem hn_zero (x : ℝ) : hn 0 x = 1 := by simp [hn_eq, He, hermR_zero]
   232	
   233	/-- `hn_1(x) = x`. -/
   234	theorem hn_one (x : ℝ) : hn 1 x = x := by
   235	  simp [hn_eq, He, hermR_succ, hermR_zero]
   236	
   237	/-- Every product `hn n * hn m` is integrable against `N(0,1)`. -/
   238	theorem integrable_hn_mul_hn (n m : ℕ) :
   239	    Integrable (fun x => hn n x * hn m x) (gaussianReal 0 1) := by
   240	  simpa [hn] using integrable_eval (hnPoly n * hnPoly m)
   241	
   242	/-- **Orthonormality** of the normalized Hermite polynomials under `N(0,1)`. -/
   243	theorem integral_hn_mul_hn (n m : ℕ) :
   244	    ∫ x, hn n x * hn m x ∂gaussianReal 0 1 = if n = m then 1 else 0 := by
   245	  have h : (fun x => hn n x * hn m x) =
   246	      fun x => ((√(n ! : ℝ))⁻¹ * (√(m ! : ℝ))⁻¹) * (He n x * He m x) := by
   247	    funext x; rw [hn_eq, hn_eq]; ring
   248	  rw [h, integral_const_mul, (integral_He_mul_He n m).2]
   249	  split_ifs with hnm
   250	  · subst hnm
   251	    have := sqrt_factorial_pos n
   252	    rw [← mul_inv, Real.mul_self_sqrt (by positivity)]
   253	    exact inv_mul_cancel₀ (by exact_mod_cast (Nat.factorial_pos n).ne')
   254	  · simp
   255	
   256	/-- **Recurrence** `x hn_n = √(n+1) hn_{n+1} + √n hn_{n-1}` (at `n = 0` the
   257	second coefficient is `0`). -/
   258	theorem mul_hn (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
   259	    x * hn n x = √((n : ℝ) + 1) * hn (n + 1) x + √(n : ℝ) * hn (n - 1) x := by
   260	  have hrec : x * He n x = He (n + 1) x + n * He (n - 1) x := by

261	    have := congrArg (eval x) (X_mul_hermR n)
   262	    simpa [He] using this
   263	  have hs : √((n + 1)! : ℝ) = √((n : ℝ) + 1) * √(n ! : ℝ) := by
   264	    rw [Nat.factorial_succ, Nat.cast_mul, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity)]; push_cast; ring
   265	  have hpos := sqrt_factorial_pos n
   266	  have h1 : 0 < √((n : ℝ) + 1) := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by positivity)
   267	  rw [hn_eq, hn_eq, hn_eq, hs]
   268	  cases n with
   269	  | zero => simp at hrec ⊢; rw [hrec]
   270	  | succ k =>
   271	    simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel] at hrec ⊢
   272	    have hs' : √((k + 1)! : ℝ) = √((k : ℝ) + 1) * √(k ! : ℝ) := by
   273	      rw [Nat.factorial_succ, Nat.cast_mul, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity)]; push_cast; ring
   274	    rw [hs'] at hpos ⊢
   275	    have hk := sqrt_factorial_pos k
   276	    have h2 : 0 < √((k : ℝ) + 1) := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by positivity)
   277	    have hsq : √((k : ℝ) + 1) * √((k : ℝ) + 1) = (k : ℝ) + 1 :=
   278	      Real.mul_self_sqrt (by positivity)
   279	    push_cast at hrec ⊢
   280	    field_simp
   281	    rw [Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity)]
   282	    linarith [hrec]

   284	/-! ### Several variables -/
   285	
   286	variable {m : ℕ}
   287	
   288	/-- The multi-index Hermite function `hk k x = ∏_i hn_{k_i}(x_i)`. -/
   289	def hk (k : Fin m → ℕ) (x : Fin m → ℝ) : ℝ := ∏ i, hn (k i) (x i)
   290	
   291	/-- The unit multi-index `e_i`. -/
   292	abbrev unitIdx (i : Fin m) : Fin m → ℕ := Pi.single i 1
   293	
   294	/-- `hk_0 = 1`. -/
   295	theorem hk_zero (x : Fin m → ℝ) : hk 0 x = 1 := by simp [hk, hn_zero]
   296	
   297	/-- `hk_{e_i}(x) = x_i`. -/
   298	theorem hk_unitIdx (i : Fin m) (x : Fin m → ℝ) : hk (unitIdx i) x = x i := by
   299	  rw [hk, ← Finset.mul_prod_erase univ _ (mem_univ i)]
   300	  rw [Finset.prod_eq_one fun j hj => by
   301	    simp [unitIdx, Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hj, hn_zero]]
   302	  simp [hn_one]
   303	
   304	/-- Every product `hk k * hk l` is integrable under `stdPi m`. -/
   305	theorem integrable_hk_mul_hk (k l : Fin m → ℕ) :
   306	    Integrable (fun x => hk k x * hk l x) (GaussianIBP.stdPi m) := by
   307	  have h : (fun x => hk k x * hk l x) = fun x => ∏ i, (hn (k i) (x i) * hn (l i) (x i)) := by
   308	    funext x; simp [hk, Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
   309	  rw [h, GaussianIBP.stdPi]
   310	  exact Integrable.fintype_prod (f := fun i y => hn (k i) y * hn (l i) y)
   311	    fun i => integrable_hn_mul_hn _ _
   312	
   313	/-- **Orthonormality** of the multi-index Hermite functions under the product
   314	Gaussian `stdPi m`. -/
   315	theorem integral_hk_mul_hk (k l : Fin m → ℕ) :
   316	    ∫ x, hk k x * hk l x ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m = if k = l then 1 else 0 := by
   317	  have h : (fun x => hk k x * hk l x) = fun x => ∏ i, (hn (k i) (x i) * hn (l i) (x i)) := by
   318	    funext x; simp [hk, Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
   319	  rw [h, GaussianIBP.stdPi,
   320	    integral_fintype_prod_eq_prod (f := fun i y => hn (k i) y * hn (l i) y)]
   321	  simp only [integral_hn_mul_hn]
   322	  rw [Finset.prod_boole]
   323	  simp [funext_iff]
   324	
   325	/-- Auxiliary: `hk` splits off coordinate `i`. -/
   326	theorem hk_eq_mul_erase (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
   327	    hk k x = hn (k i) (x i) * ∏ j ∈ univ.erase i, hn (k j) (x j) :=
   328	  (Finset.mul_prod_erase univ (fun j => hn (k j) (x j)) (mem_univ i)).symm
   329	
   330	/-- Auxiliary: changing the multi-index only at `i` changes only the `i`-th
   331	factor. -/
   332	theorem hk_eq_of_eq_off (k l : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) (hkl : ∀ j, j ≠ i → l j = k j)
   333	    (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
   334	    hk l x = hn (l i) (x i) * ∏ j ∈ univ.erase i, hn (k j) (x j) := by
   335	  rw [hk_eq_mul_erase l i]
   336	  congr 1
   337	  exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun j hj => by rw [hkl j (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hj)]
   338	
   339	/-- **Coordinate recurrence** `x_i hk_k = √(k_i+1) hk_{k+e_i} + √(k_i) hk_{k-e_i}`
   340	(truncated subtraction; at `k_i = 0` the second coefficient is `0`). -/
   341	theorem coord_mul_hk (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
   342	    x i * hk k x = √((k i : ℝ) + 1) * hk (k + unitIdx i) x +
   343	      √(k i : ℝ) * hk (k - unitIdx i) x := by
   344	  rw [hk_eq_mul_erase k i, hk_eq_of_eq_off k (k + unitIdx i) i
   345	      (fun j hj => by simp [hj]),
   346	    hk_eq_of_eq_off k (k - unitIdx i) i (fun j hj => by simp [hj])]
   347	  have h1 : (k + unitIdx i) i = k i + 1 := by simp
   348	  have h2 : (k - unitIdx i) i = k i - 1 := by simp
   349	  rw [h1, h2, ← mul_assoc, mul_hn]; ring

   351	/-! ### The spanning step -/
   352	
   353	/-- Functions on `Fin m → ℝ` that are real combinations of the `hk l` with
   354	`|l| = ∑_i l_i ≤ n`. -/
   355	def HermiteSpan (m n : ℕ) (F : (Fin m → ℝ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
   356	  ∃ c : (Fin m → ℕ) → ℝ, ∀ x, F x =
   357	    ∑ l ∈ (Fintype.piFinset fun _ => range (n + 1)).filter (fun l => ∑ i, l i ≤ n),
   358	      c l * hk l x
   359	
   360	/-- Auxiliary: one-variable span of `hn_0, …, hn_j`. -/
   361	def Span1 (j : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
   362	  ∃ b : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ x, f x = ∑ l ∈ range (j + 1), b l * hn l x
   363	
   364	/-- Auxiliary: `Span1 j` is closed under addition. -/
   365	theorem Span1.add {j : ℕ} {f g : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Span1 j f) (hg : Span1 j g) :
   366	    Span1 j (f + g) := by
   367	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hf; obtain ⟨b', hb'⟩ := hg
   368	  exact ⟨b + b', fun x => by simp [hb, hb', add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]⟩
   369	
   370	/-- Auxiliary: `Span1 j` is closed under scalar multiples. -/
   371	theorem Span1.smul {j : ℕ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (r : ℝ) (hf : Span1 j f) :
   372	    Span1 j (fun x => r * f x) := by
   373	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hf
   374	  exact ⟨fun l => r * b l, fun x => by simp [hb, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]⟩
   375	
   376	/-- Auxiliary: `Span1 j ⊆ Span1 j'` for `j ≤ j'`. -/
   377	theorem Span1.mono {j j' : ℕ} (hjj : j ≤ j') {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Span1 j f) : Span1 j' f := by
   378	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hf
   379	  refine ⟨fun l => if l ≤ j then b l else 0, fun x => ?_⟩
   380	  rw [hb, ← Finset.sum_subset (range_subset_range.2 (by omega : j + 1 ≤ j' + 1))]
   381	  · exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun l hl => by
   382	      simp at hl; simp [show l ≤ j by omega]
   383	  · intro l _ hl; simp at hl; simp [show ¬ l ≤ j by omega]
   384	
   385	/-- Auxiliary: `0 ∈ Span1 j`. -/
   386	theorem Span1.zero (j : ℕ) : Span1 j (fun _ => 0) := ⟨0, fun x => by simp⟩
   387	
   388	/-- Auxiliary: `hn l ∈ Span1 j` for `l ≤ j`. -/
   389	theorem Span1.of_hn {j l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ j) : Span1 j (hn l) :=
   390	  ⟨fun l' => if l' = l then 1 else 0, fun x => by
   391	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single l (fun b _ hb => by simp [hb]) (fun h => by simp at h; omega)]
   392	    simp⟩
   393	
   394	/-- Auxiliary: `Span1 j` is closed under finite sums. -/
   395	theorem Span1.sum {j : ℕ} {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℝ → ℝ)
   396	    (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, Span1 j (f a)) : Span1 j (fun x => ∑ a ∈ s, f a x) := by
   397	  classical
   398	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   399	  | empty => simpa using Span1.zero j
   400	  | insert a s ha ih =>
   401	    have := (hf a (mem_insert_self a s)).add (ih fun b hb => hf b (mem_insert_of_mem hb))
   402	    convert this using 1
   403	    funext x; simp [Finset.sum_insert ha]
   404	
   405	/-- Auxiliary (triangularity): `x^j` lies in the span of `hn_0, …, hn_j`. -/
   406	theorem pow_mem_span1 (j : ℕ) : Span1 j (fun x => x ^ j) := by
   407	  induction j with
   408	  | zero => exact ⟨fun l => if l = 0 then 1 else 0, fun x => by simp [hn_zero]⟩
   409	  | succ j ih =>
   410	    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := ih
   411	    have hb' : ∀ x : ℝ, x ^ j = ∑ l ∈ range (j + 1), b l * hn l x := hb
   412	    have h : (fun x : ℝ => x ^ (j + 1)) = fun x => ∑ l ∈ range (j + 1),
   413	        (b l * √((l : ℝ) + 1) * hn (l + 1) x + b l * √(l : ℝ) * hn (l - 1) x) := by
   414	      funext x
   415	      rw [pow_succ, hb', Finset.sum_mul]
   416	      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun l _ => by
   417	        rw [mul_assoc, mul_comm (hn l x) x, mul_hn]; ring
   418	    rw [h]
   419	    refine Span1.sum _ _ fun l hl => ?_
   420	    have hl' : l ≤ j := by simp at hl; omega
   421	    have := ((Span1.of_hn (j := j + 1) (l := l + 1) (by omega)).smul (b l * √((l : ℝ) + 1))).add
   422	      ((Span1.of_hn (j := j + 1) (l := l - 1) (by omega)).smul (b l * √(l : ℝ)))
   423	    convert this using 1

   425	/-- The spanning step: each monomial `x^k = ∏_i x_i^{k_i}` with `|k| ≤ n` lies
   426	in `HermiteSpan m n`. -/
   427	theorem monomial_mem_hermiteSpan (n : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ) (hdk : ∑ i, k i ≤ n) :
   428	    HermiteSpan m n (fun x => ∏ i, x i ^ k i) := by
   429	  classical
   430	  choose b hb using fun i => pow_mem_span1 (k i)
   431	  simp only at hb
   432	  set S := Fintype.piFinset fun i => range (k i + 1) with hS
   433	  set D := (Fintype.piFinset fun _ : Fin m => range (n + 1)).filter (fun l => ∑ i, l i ≤ n)
   434	  have hSD : S ⊆ D := by
   435	    intro l hl
   436	    simp only [hS, Fintype.mem_piFinset, mem_range] at hl
   437	    have hle : ∑ i, l i ≤ n := (Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => by have := hl i; omega).trans hdk
   438	    simp only [D, mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset, mem_range]
   439	    exact ⟨fun i => by
   440	      have := Finset.single_le_sum (fun j _ => Nat.zero_le (l j)) (mem_univ i)
   441	      omega, hle⟩
   442	  refine ⟨fun l => if l ∈ S then ∏ i, b i (l i) else 0, fun x => ?_⟩
   443	  have h1 : ∏ i, x i ^ k i = ∑ l ∈ S, (∏ i, b i (l i)) * hk l x := by
   444	    rw [Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => hb i (x i), Finset.prod_univ_sum]
   445	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun l _ => by simp [hk, Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
   446	  show ∏ i, x i ^ k i = _
   447	  rw [h1, ← Finset.sum_subset hSD]
   448	  · exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun l hl => by simp only [hl, ite_true]
   449	  · intro l _ hl; simp only [hl, ite_false, zero_mul]
   450	
   451	/-- `HermiteSpan m n` is closed under addition. -/
   452	theorem HermiteSpan.add {n : ℕ} {F G : (Fin m → ℝ) → ℝ} (hF : HermiteSpan m n F)
   453	    (hG : HermiteSpan m n G) : HermiteSpan m n (fun x => F x + G x) := by
   454	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hF; obtain ⟨c', hc'⟩ := hG
   455	  exact ⟨c + c', fun x => by simp [hc, hc', add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]⟩
   456	
   457	/-- `HermiteSpan m n` is closed under scalar multiples. -/
   458	theorem HermiteSpan.smul {n : ℕ} {F : (Fin m → ℝ) → ℝ} (r : ℝ) (hF : HermiteSpan m n F) :
   459	    HermiteSpan m n (fun x => r * F x) := by
   460	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hF
   461	  exact ⟨fun l => r * c l, fun x => by simp [hc, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]⟩
   462	
   463	/-- `0 ∈ HermiteSpan m n`. -/
   464	theorem HermiteSpan.zero (n : ℕ) : HermiteSpan m n (fun _ => 0) := ⟨0, fun x => by simp⟩
   465	
   466	/-- `HermiteSpan m n` is closed under finite sums. -/
   467	theorem HermiteSpan.sum {n : ℕ} {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (F : ι → (Fin m → ℝ) → ℝ)
   468	    (hF : ∀ a ∈ s, HermiteSpan m n (F a)) : HermiteSpan m n (fun x => ∑ a ∈ s, F a x) := by
   469	  classical
   470	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   471	  | empty => simpa using HermiteSpan.zero (m := m) n
   472	  | insert a s ha ih =>
   473	    have := (hF a (mem_insert_self a s)).add (ih fun b hb => hF b (mem_insert_of_mem hb))
   474	    convert this using 1
   475	    funext x; simp [Finset.sum_insert ha]
   476	
   477	/-- The spanning step for polynomials: every real polynomial in `x_1, …, x_m` of
   478	total degree at most `n` is, as a function, a real combination of the `hk l`
   479	with `|l| ≤ n`. -/
   480	theorem mvPolynomial_mem_hermiteSpan (n : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) ℝ)
   481	    (hp : p.totalDegree ≤ n) : HermiteSpan m n (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p) := by
   482	  classical
   483	  have key : ∀ s ∈ p.support, HermiteSpan m n
   484	      (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.monomial s (p.coeff s))) := by
   485	    intro s hs
   486	    have hdeg : ∑ i, s i ≤ n := by
   487	      have := MvPolynomial.le_totalDegree hs
   488	      rw [Finsupp.sum_fintype _ _ (fun _ => rfl)] at this
   489	      exact this.trans hp
   490	    have := (monomial_mem_hermiteSpan n (fun i => s i) hdeg).smul (p.coeff s)
   491	    convert this using 2 with x
   492	    rw [MvPolynomial.eval_monomial, Finsupp.prod_fintype _ _ (fun _ => by simp)]
   493	  have hsum : (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x p) = fun x => ∑ s ∈ p.support,
   494	      MvPolynomial.eval x (MvPolynomial.monomial s (p.coeff s)) := by
   495	    funext x
   496	    conv_lhs => rw [p.as_sum]
   497	    rw [map_sum]
   498	  rw [hsum]
   499	  exact HermiteSpan.sum _ _ key

     5	variable {C B V : Type} [DecidableEq C]
     6	
     7	def bump (i : C) (d : C → Nat) : C → Nat :=
     8	  fun c => d c + if c = i then 1 else 0
     9	
    10	def counts : List (C × B) → C → Nat
    11	  | [] => fun _ => 0
    12	  | (i, _) :: w => bump i (counts w)
    13	
    14	def raw (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (v₀ : V) : List (C × B) → V
    15	  | [] => v₀
    16	  | (i, b) :: w => F b (J i (raw J F v₀ w))
    17	
    18	def cut (P : V → V) (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V)
    19	    (v₀ : V) : List (C × B) → V
    20	  | [] => v₀
    21	  | (i, b) :: w => F b (P (J i (P (cut P J F v₀ w))))
    22	
    23	theorem raw_support
    24	    (Good : (C → Nat) → V → Prop)
    25	    (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (v₀ : V)
    26	    (hv₀ : Good (fun _ => 0) v₀)
    27	    (hJ : ∀ d i v, Good d v → Good (bump i d) (J i v))
    28	    (hF : ∀ d b v, Good d v → Good d (F b v))
    29	    (w : List (C × B)) : Good (counts w) (raw J F v₀ w) := by
    30	  induction w with
    31	  | nil => exact hv₀
    32	  | cons a w ih =>
    33	    exact hF _ a.2 _ (hJ _ a.1 _ ih)
    34	
    35	theorem cut_eq_raw
    36	    (Good : (C → Nat) → V → Prop)
    37	    (J : C → V → V) (F : B → V → V) (P : V → V)
    38	    (v₀ : V) (N : C → Nat)
    39	    (hv₀ : Good (fun _ => 0) v₀)
    40	    (hJ : ∀ d i v, Good d v → Good (bump i d) (J i v))
    41	    (hF : ∀ d b v, Good d v → Good d (F b v))
    42	    (hP : ∀ d v, (∀ c, d c ≤ N c) → Good d v → P v = v)
    43	    (w : List (C × B)) (hN : ∀ c, counts w c ≤ N c) :
    44	    cut P J F v₀ w = raw J F v₀ w := by
    45	  induction w with
    46	  | nil => rfl
    47	  | cons a w ih =>
    48	    have hs : ∀ c, counts w c ≤ N c := by
    49	      intro c
    50	      have hc := hN c
    51	      simp only [counts, bump] at hc
    52	      omega
    53	    have hw := raw_support Good J F v₀ hv₀ hJ hF w
    54	    have hp₀ := hP (counts w) (raw J F v₀ w) hs hw
    55	    have hp₁ := hP (bump a.1 (counts w)) (J a.1 (raw J F v₀ w))
    56	      hN (hJ _ _ _ hw)
    57	    change F a.2 (P (J a.1 (P (cut P J F v₀ w)))) =
    58	      F a.2 (J a.1 (raw J F v₀ w))
    59	    rw [ih hs, hp₀, hp₁]
    60	
    61	end StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord

     6	-- Coefficients in the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite basis:
     7	-- x He_n = He_(n+1) + n He_(n-1). This defines the finite recurrence;
     8	-- no assertion about Gaussian L² or polynomial realization is imported.
     9	private def vacuum (n : Nat) : Nat := if n = 0 then 1 else 0
    10	private def insert (_ : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat :=
    11	  (if n = 0 then 0 else p (n-1)) + (n+1) * p (n+1)
    12	private def frame (_ : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat) := p
    13	private def project (N : Nat) (p : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) :=
    14	  if n ≤ N then p n else 0
    15	private def Good (d : Unit → Nat) (p : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
    16	  ∀ n, d () < n → p n = 0
    17	
    18	private theorem vacuum_good : Good (fun _ => 0) vacuum := by
    19	  intro n hn
    20	  simp only [vacuum]
    21	  split <;> omega
    22	
    23	private theorem insert_good (d : Unit → Nat) (i : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat)
    24	    (hp : Good d p) : Good (bump i d) (insert i p) := by
    25	  intro n hn
    26	  have hi : i = () := by cases i; rfl
    27	  subst i
    28	  simp [bump] at hn
    29	  have h₁ : p (n-1) = 0 := hp _ (by omega)
    30	  have h₂ : p (n+1) = 0 := hp _ (by omega)
    31	  simp [insert, h₁, h₂]
    32	
    33	private theorem frame_good (d : Unit → Nat) (b : Unit) (p : Nat → Nat)
    34	    (hp : Good d p) : Good d (frame b p) := hp
    35	
    36	private theorem project_fixes (N : Nat) (d : Unit → Nat) (p : Nat → Nat)
    37	    (hd : ∀ c, d c ≤ N) (hp : Good d p) : project N p = p := by
    38	  funext n
    39	  simp only [project]
    40	  split
    41	  · rfl
    42	  · exact (hp n (by have h := hd (); omega)).symm
    43	
    44	private theorem count_length (w : List (Unit × Unit)) : counts w () = w.length := by
    45	  induction w with
    46	  | nil => rfl
    47	  | cons a w ih =>
    48	    have ha : a.1 = () := by cases a with | mk i b => cases i; rfl
    49	    simp [counts, bump, ha, ih]
    50	
    51	-- Actual recurrence consumer, arbitrary word length and cutoff; not a third
    52	-- public claim and not the analytic Hermite/Hilbert realization theorem.
    53	example (w : List (Unit × Unit)) (N : Nat) (hN : w.length ≤ N) :
    54	    cut (project N) insert frame vacuum w = raw insert frame vacuum w := by
    55	  apply cut_eq_raw Good insert frame (project N) vacuum (fun _ => N)
    56	    vacuum_good insert_good frame_good (project_fixes N) w
    57	  intro c
    58	  cases c
    59	  simpa only [count_length] using hN
    60	
    61	-- Four insertions preserve the vacuum self-contraction 3 at cutoff 4.
    62	example : cut (project 4) insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()), ((),()), ((),()) ] 0 = 3 := by
    63	  decide
    64	-- An insufficient cutoff actually changes the second-order vector.
    65	example : cut (project 1) insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 2 = 0 := by decide
    66	example : raw insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 2 = 1 := by decide
    67	-- Removing lowering loses the self-contraction, so creation-only is false.
    68	example : raw insert frame vacuum [ ((),()), ((),()) ] 0 = 1 := by decide
    69	
    70	end StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWordConsumer

    77	/-! ### Multi-indices -/
    78	
    79	/-- The total degree `|k| = ∑_i k_i` of a multi-index. -/
    80	def deg (k : Fin m → ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ i, k i
    81	
    82	/-- The multi-indices of total degree at most `N`. -/
    83	def degLE (m N : ℕ) : Finset (Fin m → ℕ) :=
    84	  (Fintype.piFinset fun _ => range (N + 1)).filter fun k => ∑ i, k i ≤ N
    85	
    86	/-- Membership in `degLE m N` is `|k| ≤ N`. -/
    87	theorem mem_degLE {N : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} : k ∈ degLE m N ↔ deg k ≤ N := by
    88	  simp only [degLE, mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset, mem_range, deg]
    89	  refine ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨fun i => ?_, h⟩⟩
    90	  have := Finset.single_le_sum (fun j _ => Nat.zero_le (k j)) (mem_univ i)
    91	  omega
    92	
    93	/-- Auxiliary: `degLE m N ⊆ degLE m M` for `N ≤ M`. -/
    94	theorem degLE_mono {N M : ℕ} (h : N ≤ M) : degLE m N ⊆ degLE m M :=
    95	  fun _ hk => mem_degLE.2 ((mem_degLE.1 hk).trans h)
    96	
    97	/-- Auxiliary: `0 ∈ degLE m N`. -/
    98	theorem zero_mem_degLE (N : ℕ) : (0 : Fin m → ℕ) ∈ degLE m N := mem_degLE.2 (by simp [deg])
    99	
   100	/-- Auxiliary: `|k + e_i| = |k| + 1`. -/
   101	theorem deg_add_unitIdx (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : deg (k + unitIdx i) = deg k + 1 := by
   102	  simp [deg, Finset.sum_add_distrib, unitIdx]
   103	
   104	/-- Auxiliary: `(k - e_i) + e_i = k` when `k_i ≠ 0`. -/
   105	theorem sub_add_unitIdx {k : Fin m → ℕ} {i : Fin m} (h : k i ≠ 0) :
   106	    k - unitIdx i + unitIdx i = k := by
   107	  funext j
   108	  by_cases hj : j = i
   109	  · subst hj; simp; omega
   110	  · simp [unitIdx, hj]
   111	
   112	/-- Auxiliary: `(k + e_i) - e_i = k`. -/
   113	theorem add_sub_unitIdx (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : k + unitIdx i - unitIdx i = k := by
   114	  funext j; simp
   115	
   116	/-- Auxiliary: `|k - e_i| + 1 = |k|` when `k_i ≠ 0`. -/
   117	theorem deg_sub_unitIdx {k : Fin m → ℕ} {i : Fin m} (h : k i ≠ 0) :
   118	    deg (k - unitIdx i) + 1 = deg k := by
   119	  conv_rhs => rw [← sub_add_unitIdx h]
   120	  rw [deg_add_unitIdx]

   122	/-- Auxiliary: `(k - e_i)_i = k_i - 1`. -/
   123	theorem sub_unitIdx_apply (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : (k - unitIdx i) i = k i - 1 := by
   124	  simp
   125	
   126	/-- Auxiliary: `(k + e_i)_i = k_i + 1`. -/
   127	theorem add_unitIdx_apply (k : Fin m → ℕ) (i : Fin m) : (k + unitIdx i) i = k i + 1 := by
   128	  simp

   132	theorem sum_degLE_succ_eq (i : Fin m) (N : ℕ) {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
   133	    (g : (Fin m → ℕ) → M) (hg : ∀ k, k i = 0 → g k = 0) :
   134	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), g k = ∑ j ∈ degLE m N, g (j + unitIdx i) := by

   138	  refine Finset.sum_nbij' (fun j => j + unitIdx i) (fun k => k - unitIdx i) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_

   141	    refine ⟨mem_degLE.2 ?_, by simp⟩
   142	    rw [deg_add_unitIdx]; have := mem_degLE.1 hj; omega

   145	    have h1 := deg_sub_unitIdx hk.2
   146	    have h2 := mem_degLE.1 hk.1

   148	  · intro j _; exact add_sub_unitIdx j i
   149	  · intro k hk
   150	    simp only [mem_filter] at hk

   152	  · intro j _; rfl

   154	/-- Auxiliary: a function vanishing in degrees above `N` has the same sum over
   155	`degLE m M` for every `M ≥ N`. -/
   156	theorem sum_degLE_eq_of_vanish {N M : ℕ} (hNM : N ≤ M) {E : Type*} [AddCommMonoid E]
   157	    (g : (Fin m → ℕ) → E) (hg : ∀ k, N < deg k → g k = 0) :
   158	    ∑ k ∈ degLE m M, g k = ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, g k := by

   163	/-! ### Coefficient operators -/
   164	
   165	variable {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℂ X]
   166	
   167	/-- A coefficient vector vanishes in degrees above `N`. -/
   168	def Supp (N : ℕ) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) : Prop := ∀ k, N < deg k → v k = 0
   169	
   170	/-- The annihilation operator `(a_i v)_k = √(k_i+1) v_{k+e_i}`. -/
   171	def ann (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   172	  (Real.sqrt ((k i : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) • v (k + unitIdx i)
   173	
   174	/-- The creation operator `(a_i^* v)_k = √(k_i) v_{k-e_i}`. -/
   175	def cre (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   176	  (Real.sqrt (k i : ℝ) : ℂ) • v (k - unitIdx i)
   177	
   178	/-- Multiplication by the coordinate `g_i` on coefficients, `a_i^* + a_i`. -/
   179	def gmul (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X := cre i v k + ann i v k
   180	
   181	/-- The creation row `(u_i)_i ↦ ∑_i a_i^* u_i`. -/
   182	def creRow (u : Fin m → (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X := ∑ i, cre i (u i) k
   183	
   184	/-- The field operator `∑_i (a_i^* + a_i) ⊗ H_i` on coefficients. -/
   185	def fieldOp (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) (k : Fin m → ℕ) : X :=
   186	  ∑ i, gmul i (fun l => H i (v l)) k
   187	
   188	/-- The vacuum vector `1 ⊗ u` (coefficient `u` at `k = 0`). -/
   189	def vac (u : X) : (Fin m → ℕ) → X := fun k => if k = 0 then u else 0
   190	
   191	/-- Auxiliary: `(a_i^* v)_k = 0` when `k_i = 0`. -/
   192	theorem cre_of_eq_zero (i : Fin m) (v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X) {k : Fin m → ℕ} (h : k i = 0) :
   193	    cre i v k = 0 := by simp [cre, h]

   298	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]

   311	      ((N : ℝ) + 1) * c * ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), ‖v k‖ ^ 2 := by

   314	  set V := ∑ k ∈ degLE m (N + 1), ‖v k‖ ^ 2

   317	      intro k
   318	      rw [@norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ]

   320	      have : inner ℂ (a k) (a k) = ∑ i, inner ℂ (ann i (fun l => H i (v l)) k) (a k) := by
   321	        show inner ℂ (annOp H v k) (a k) = _
   322	        rw [annOp, sum_inner]

   325	      simp only [ann, inner_smul_left, hH]
   326	    simp only [S, e1, ← map_sum]

   328	    simp only [sum_inner_ann]
   329	    rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   330	    congr 1

331	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => ?_
   332	    rw [creOp, creRow, inner_sum]

   518	  ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, (hk k x : ℂ) • v k

   523	    Integrable (fun x => ‖iota N v x‖ ^ 2) (GaussianIBP.stdPi m) ∧

   531	  classical
   532	  rw [iota, Finset.sum_eq_single (0 : Fin m → ℕ) (fun k _ hk => by simp [vac, hk])

   536	/-- **Coordinate multiplication** on the expansion: for `v` supported in degrees

   539	    (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
   540	    ((x i : ℝ) : ℂ) • iota N v x = iota (N + 1) (gmul i v) x := by
   541	  -- left side, split by the coordinate recurrence

   543	      ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ((Real.sqrt ((k i : ℝ) + 1) * hk (k + unitIdx i) x : ℝ) : ℂ) • v k +
   544	      ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ((Real.sqrt (k i : ℝ) * hk (k - unitIdx i) x : ℝ) : ℂ) • v k := by
   545	    rw [iota, Finset.smul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   546	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun k _ => ?_
   547	    rw [smul_smul, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, GaussianHermite.coord_mul_hk, Complex.ofReal_add,

   551	      ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ((Real.sqrt ((k i : ℝ) + 1) * hk (k + unitIdx i) x : ℝ) : ℂ) • v k := by
   552	    rw [sum_degLE_succ_eq i N _ (fun k hk => by simp [cre_of_eq_zero i v hk])]

   554	    simp only [cre, add_unitIdx_apply, add_sub_unitIdx, smul_smul]

   559	    have h1 : ∑ k ∈ degLE m N, ((Real.sqrt (k i : ℝ) * hk (k - unitIdx i) x : ℝ) : ℂ) • v k =

   583	theorem sum_coord_smul_iota (N : ℕ) (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X) {v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X}

   598	    (hH : ∀ i u w, inner ℂ (H i u) w = inner ℂ u (H i w)) {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 ≤ c)

   604	        (2 * Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) + 1) * Real.sqrt c) ^ 2 *
   605	          ∫ x, ‖iota N v x‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m := by
   606	  simp only [sum_coord_smul_iota N H hv]
   607	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := integral_norm_sq_iota (N + 1) (fieldOp H v)

   613	`∫ ‖iota N (fieldOp H v) x‖² dγ_m ≤ (2√(N+1)√c)² ∫ ‖iota N v x‖² dγ_m`. -/
   614	theorem gaussian_field_bound_trunc (N : ℕ) (H : Fin m → X →L[ℂ] X)
   615	    (hH : ∀ i u w, inner ℂ (H i u) w = inner ℂ u (H i w)) {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 ≤ c)
   616	    (hc : ∀ u, ∑ i, ‖H i u‖ ^ 2 ≤ c * ‖u‖ ^ 2) {v : (Fin m → ℕ) → X} (hv : Supp N v) :

   618	      ∫ x, ‖iota N (fieldOp H v) x‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m ≤

   620	          ∫ x, ‖iota N v x‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m := by

   628	theorem vacuum_insertion_isometry (w : Fin m → X) :

   630	      ∫ x, ‖∑ i, ((x i : ℝ) : ℂ) • w i‖ ^ 2 ∂GaussianIBP.stdPi m = ∑ i, ‖w i‖ ^ 2 := by

   632	    (GaussianHermite.hk_unitIdx i x).symm

   634	    (fun i _ j _ => by
   635	      simpa [hx] using GaussianHermite.integrable_hk_mul_hk (unitIdx i) (unitIdx j))
   636	    (fun i _ j _ => by
   637	      simp only [hx, GaussianHermite.integral_hk_mul_hk]
   638	      simp [unitIdx, Pi.single_left_inj (one_ne_zero (α := ℕ))])

   517	    GoodDeg (fun c => d c + if c = i then 1 else 0) (gmul i (fun l => K i (v l))) := by

   519	  have h1 : v (k + unitIdx i) = 0 := hv _ ⟨c, by
   520	    by_cases hci : c = i
   521	    · subst hci; simp at hc ⊢; omega
   522	    · simp [hci] at hc ⊢; omega⟩
   523	  have h2 : v (k - unitIdx i) = 0 := hv _ ⟨c, by
   524	    by_cases hci : c = i
   525	    · subst hci; simp at hc ⊢; omega

     3	  226|   Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
     4	  227|   nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
     5	  228|   $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
     6	  229|   convention
     7	  230|   \[
     8	  231|     \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
     9	  232|     \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
    10	  233|   \]
    11	  234|   The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
    12	  235|   when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
    13	  236|   $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
    14	  237|   \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
    15	  238|     \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
    16	  239|   \end{equation}
    17	  240|   with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
    18	  241|   includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
    19	  242| \end{hypothesis}

    22	  803| \begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
    23	  804|   \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
    24	  805|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
    25	  806|   in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
    26	  807|   $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
    27	  808|   \[
    28	  809|     N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
    29	  810|     N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
    30	  811|     N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
    31	  812|     \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
    32	  813|   \]
    33	  814|   Let
    34	  815|   \[
    35	  816|     K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
    36	  817|     \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
    37	  818|   \]
    38	  819|   Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
    39	  820|   $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
    40	  821|   $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
    41	  822|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
    42	  823|     N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
    43	  824|     N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
    44	  825|   \end{equation}
    45	  826|   More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
    46	  827|   $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
    47	  828|   by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
    48	  829|   $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
    49	  830|   and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
    50	  831|   \[
    51	  832|     K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
    52	  833|     \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
    53	  834|   \]
    54	  835|   Then, for every $\theta>0$,
    55	  836|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
    56	  837|     \begin{split}
    57	  838|       0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
    58	  839|       0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
    59	  840|     \end{split}
    60	  841|   \end{equation}
    61	  842|   These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
    62	  843|   domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
    63	  844|   scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
    64	  845|   Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
    65	  846|   give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
    66	  847|   unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.
    67	  848| \end{lemma}
    68	  849| 
    69	  850| \begin{proof}
    70	  851|   Scaling the Fourier representation of $\Gamma$ and using Fourier uniqueness
    71	  852|   gives $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. Radon finiteness and $\alpha > 0$ then imply
    72	  853|   $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$. In particular, $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha V$, where $V = \mu(B_1)
    73	  854|   < \infty$. Therefore, for $a > 0$,
    74	  855|   \[
    75	  856|     \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{a^2+|\xi|^2}
    76	  857|     =\alpha V a^{\alpha-2}
    77	  858|     \int_0^\infty\frac{u^{\alpha-1}}{1+u^2}\ud u<\infty.
    78	  859|   \]
    79	  860|   The last integral is finite since $0 < \alpha < 2$. Substitution into $N_1$
    80	  861|   reduces its finiteness to
    81	  862|   $\int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}(\theta+\lambda)^{\alpha-2} \ud\lambda <
    82	  863|   \infty$: the conditions at zero and infinity are $\alpha_0 > 0$ and
    83	  864|   $\alpha+\alpha_0 < 2$.
    84	  865| 
    85	  866|   For $N_2$ use $|\widehat{G}_s(\xi)| \le \min(s,|\xi|^{-1})$. On $|\xi| \le 1$,
    86	  867|   absolute integration is bounded by
    87	  868|   \[
    88	  869|     V\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
    89	  870|     e^{-\theta(s+t)}|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}st\ud s\ud t<\infty.
    90	  871|   \]
    91	  872|   On $|\xi| > 1$, use $\int_{|\xi|>1}|\xi|^{-2}\mu(\ud\xi) = \alpha
    92	  873|   V/(2-\alpha)$ and the same time integral without $st$. Both time integrals are
    93	  874|   finite by splitting into $s \le t$ and $t \le s$, then using $u = \min(s,t)$
    94	  875|   and $v = |s-t|$; the only singular factor is $v^{-\alpha_0}$, with $\alpha_0 <
    95	  876|   1$. This proves absolute integrability of the displayed spectral formula. For
    96	  877|   each $\xi$, its time integral is nonnegative because the temporal kernel is
    97	  878|   positive definite. Indeed, it is a positive Laplace mixture of the kernels
    98	  879|   $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$. This proves $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$.

   101	  882|   change $\lambda = \theta u$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$. In $N_2$ change $s =
   102	  883|   u/\theta$, $t = v/\theta$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$, using
   103	  884|   $\widehat{G}_{u/\theta}(\theta\eta) = \theta^{-1}\widehat{G}_u(\eta)$. These
   104	  885|   changes give exactly the stated powers.

   107	  888|   nonnegative $N_1(1)$ integral. For the second, $0 \le K_M(r) \le
   108	  889|   |r|^{-\alpha_0}$ and $K_M(r) \to 0$ for $r \ne 0$. The absolute majorant just
   109	  890|   proved permits dominated convergence in $(s,t,\xi)$, giving $N_2^{(M)}(1)^2
   110	  891|   \to 0$. The tail kernel is positive definite by the same Laplace-mixture
   111	  892|   argument, so its quadratic form is nonnegative.
   112	  893| 
   113	  894|   For the multiplier comparisons, define
   114	  895|   \[
   115	  896|     B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   116	  897|     e^{-\theta(s+t)}e^{-\lambda|s-t|}
   117	  898|     \widehat G_s(\xi)\overline{\widehat G_t(\xi)}\ud s\ud t.
   118	  899|   \]
   119	  900|   For each $\lambda>0$ and $\xi$, the positive definiteness of

   122	  903|   $0\le K_S\le|\cdot|^{-\alpha_0}$ justify changing the integration order:

   124	  905|     N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2
   125	  906|     =\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   126	  907|     \int_S\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}
   127	  908|     \int m(\xi)B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)\mu(\ud\xi)\ud\lambda.
   128	  909|   \]
   129	  910|   Nonnegativity now proves the second comparison

   132	  913|   comparison follows directly from the nonnegative integrand defining $N_1$.

   138	  919| \end{proof}

   192	 2043| \section{A static phase estimate at first variance order}
   193	 2044| \label{S:static-phase}
   194	 2045| 
   195	 2046| A time-block argument would have to carry both position and velocity. We
   196	 2047| establish a uniform estimate for the first variance coefficient with arbitrary
   197	 2048| deterministic initial phase. The covariance may be any member of the original
   198	 2049| three-dimensional class; no endpoint representation is assumed. The estimate
   199	 2050| below is not an all-order propagator bound.
   200	 2051| 
   201	 2052| 
   202	 2053| 
   203	 2054| Let $0 < \alpha < 2$, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonnegative, even, positive-definite
   204	 2055| tempered Radon covariance on $\R^3$, satisfying $\Gamma(rA) =
   205	 2056| r^{3-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$. Its spectral convention is $\Gamma = \int e^{i\xi\cdot
   206	 2057| x}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Put
   207	 2058| \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-constants}
   208	 2059|   \begin{split}
   209	 2060|     V&=\mu(B_1),\qquad M=\Gamma(B_1),\qquad
   210	 2061|     R_\alpha=\frac{\alpha\pi V}{2\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},\\
   211	 2062|     c_\Gamma&=\frac{(3-\alpha)M}{4\pi},\qquad
   212	 2063|     b_\alpha=2^\alpha+\frac{3^{2-\alpha}}{2-\alpha},\qquad
   213	 2064|     D_\Gamma=c_\Gamma b_\alpha.
   214	 2065|   \end{split}
   215	 2066| \end{equation}
   216	 2067| Here $B_1$ is the open unit ball in the relevant variable. The physical mass $M$
   217	 2068| and the spectral mass $V$ are not identified. Let $p_\epsilon$ be the Brownian
   218	 2069| Gaussian density with covariance $\epsilon I$, and set $\Gamma_\epsilon =
   219	 2070| p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$.
   220	 2071| 
   221	 2072| \begin{lemma}[Two static contraction bounds]\label{L:phase-contractions}
   222	 2073|   For $\lambda > 0$, $q \in \R^3$, $a > 0$, and $\epsilon > 0$,
   223	 2074|   \begin{align}
   224	 2075|     \int_{\R^3}\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\lambda^2+|q+\xi|^2}
   225	 2076|     &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},
   226	 2077|     \label{E:phase-resolvent}\\
   227	 2078|     \left|T_\epsilon(a,q)\right|
   228	 2079|     &\le D_\Gamma a^{1-\alpha},
   229	 2080|     \label{E:phase-trace}\\
   230	 2081|     T_\epsilon(a,q)
   231	 2082|     &:=\int_{\R^3}e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)
   232	 2083|     =\int_{\R^3}\widehat{G}_a(q+\xi)e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}
   233	 2084|     \mu(\ud\xi).\nonumber
   234	 2085|   \end{align}
   235	 2086| \end{lemma}
   236	 2087| 
   237	 2088| \begin{proof}
   238	 2089|   Homogeneity and Fourier uniqueness give $\mu(B_r) = Vr^\alpha$. In particular,
   239	 2090|   there is no origin atom. For $s > 0$, Schwartz Fourier pairing yields
   240	 2091|   \[
   241	 2092|     \int e^{-s|q+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
   242	 2093|     =\int p_{2s}(x)e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
   243	 2094|     \le\int p_{2s}(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
   244	 2095|     =\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
   245	 2096|   \]
   246	 2097|   The integrals are finite. Evenness makes the middle integral real, and
   247	 2098|   nonnegativity of $\Gamma$ gives the inequality. Multiply by $e^{-\lambda^2s}$
   248	 2099|   and integrate in $s$. Nonnegative Tonelli on the spectral side gives the
   249	 2100|   resolvent comparison. At $q = 0$ its value is
   250	 2101|   \[
   251	 2102|     \alpha V\int_0^\infty\frac{r^{\alpha-1}}{\lambda^2+r^2}\ud r
   252	 2103|     =R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2}.
   253	 2104|   \]
   254	 2105|   This proves~\eqref{E:phase-resolvent}.
   255	 2106| 
   256	 2107|   Since $\mu$ is tempered, its Gaussian weighting is finite. Fourier Fubini
   257	 2108|   therefore gives the identity for $T_\epsilon$. The measure
   258	 2109|   $\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)$ is finite and nonnegative, whence
   259	 2110|   $|T_\epsilon(a,q)| \le T_\epsilon(a,0)$. The radial distribution function of
   260	 2111|   $\Gamma$ is $\Gamma(B_r) = Mr^{3-\alpha}$. Thus, for every nonnegative radial
   261	 2112|   Schwartz function $F$,
   262	 2113|   \[
   263	 2114|     \int F(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
   264	 2115|     =(3-\alpha)M\int_0^\infty F(r)r^{2-\alpha}\ud r
   265	 2116|     =c_\Gamma\int_{\R^3}F(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\ud x.
   266	 2117|   \]
   267	 2118|   Apply this to $F = G_a*p_{2\epsilon}$, which is radial and Schwartz.
   268	 2119|   Nonnegative Fubini gives
   269	 2120|   \[
   270	 2121|     T_\epsilon(a,0)
   271	 2122|     =c_\Gamma[p_{2\epsilon}*(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})](0)
   272	 2123|     \le c_\Gamma\sup_z(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z).
   273	 2124|   \]
   274	 2125|   Write $r = |z|$. The spherical wave measure has mass $a$, and direct
   275	 2126|   integration over its normal coordinate gives, for $r > 0$,
   276	 2127|   \[
   277	 2128|     (G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})(z)
   278	 2129|     =\frac{(a+r)^{2-\alpha}-|a-r|^{2-\alpha}}
   279	 2130|     {2r(2-\alpha)}.
   280	 2131|   \]
   281	 2132|   For $r < a/2$, distances from $z$ to the sphere are at least $a/2$, giving the
   282	 2133|   bound $2^\alpha a^{1-\alpha}$. For $r > 2a$, they are at least $a$, giving
   283	 2134|   $a^{1-\alpha}$. On $a/2 \le r \le 2a$, the displayed formula is at most
   284	 2135|   $3^{2-\alpha}a^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$. These bounds also cover the endpoints
   285	 2136|   by continuity and give~\eqref{E:phase-trace}. This proves
   286	 2137|   Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}.
   287	 2138| \end{proof}

  2541	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  2542	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2543	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  2544	    \begin{split}
  2545	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2546	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  2547	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2548	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  2549	    \end{split}
  2550	  \end{equation}
  2551	  The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
  2552	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
  2553	\end{lemma}
  2554	
  2555	\begin{proof}
  2556	  In normalized Hermite coordinates, multiplication by $g_{ij}$ maps
  2557	  $h_{\boldsymbol a}$ to $\sqrt{a_{ij}+1}\,h_{\boldsymbol a+e_{ij}}
  2558	  +\sqrt{a_{ij}}\,h_{\boldsymbol a-e_{ij}}$; the second term is zero if $a_{ij}
  2559	  = 0$. Thus, it changes the total degree of color $i$ by one and leaves all
  2560	  other color degrees unchanged. The operators $I\otimes F_l$ leave every
  2561	  Gaussian degree unchanged. After the first $l$ insertions, the uncompressed
  2562	  word therefore has color-$i$ degree at most $r_i(l) = |\{j\le l:i_j=i\}| \le
  2563	  r_i \le N_i$. This is an induction starting from degree zero in every color.
  2564	  Consequently, $P$ is the identity both before and after every insertion along
  2565	  that word. Induction on $l$ now proves \eqref{E:finite-word-cutoff}. The
  2566	  lowering term has been retained: the assertion includes creation followed by
  2567	  annihilation and all resulting self-contractions. Linearity and equality of
  2568	  the vector integrands prove the last assertion. This is an equality of
  2569	  selected finite words, not of full propagators at a fixed cutoff. This proves
  2570	  Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff}.
  2571	\end{proof}

  2580	  Schwartz $f,g$, let $Z_n^\epsilon(h)$ be the $n$th regularized static Duhamel

  2828	\begin{lemma}[Dimension-independent Gaussian contractions]
  2829	  \label{L:interval-contractions}
  2830	  Uniformly in positive spatial smoothing and in finite Gaussian-mode and
  2831	  spatial Fourier-band cutoffs,
  2832	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-column}
  2833	    \sum_m\|A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}f\|_2^2
  2834	    \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}\|f\|_2^2.
  2835	  \end{equation}

  2837	  representation of $W(p_\epsilon(x-\cdot))$, whose covariance is
  2838	  $\Gamma_\epsilon = p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$. Consequently, on a Gaussian color
  2839	  that is initially in its vacuum, the phase insertion
  2840	  $(u,v)\mapsto(0,W_\epsilon u)$ has norm at most
  2841	  $\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{(\alpha-2)/2}$ into its Gaussian $L^2$ phase. With
  2842	  Hermite degree of this color truncated at $N$, its sandwiched field has
  2843	  operator norm at most
  2844	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-fock}
  2845	    2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{\alpha/2-2}.

  2852	  comparison in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions} uses no dimension-specific
  2853	  identity:
  2854	  \[
  2855	    \int e^{-s|\eta+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
  2856	    =\int p_{2s}^{(d)}(x)e^{i\eta\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
  2857	    \le\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).

  2860	  inequality. Integrating against $e^{-\rho^2s}\ud s$ and using radial spectral
  2861	  homogeneity yields
  2862	  \[
  2863	    \sup_\eta\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}
  2864	    \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}.
  2865	  \]

  2867	
  2868	  Gaussian isometry and unnormalized spatial Plancherel give
  2869	  \[
  2870	    \sum_m\|A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}f\|_2^2
  2871	    =\frac1{(2\pi)^d}\int|\widehat{f}(\eta)|^2
  2872	    \left(\int\frac{e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)}
  2873	    {\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}\right)\ud\eta .

  2876	  sub-sum. For a Fourier-band projection $S_b$, which commutes with $A_\rho$,

  2880	  of~\eqref{E:interval-column}, and its input is independent of this color.

  2883	  \[

  3516	  \]
  3517	  The first metric factor occurs on only one copy; the last costs at most one
  3518	  factor on each copy. To justify the length substitution, expand the entire
  3519	  higher-degree weight, before its positive constant:
  3520	  \[
  3521	    h^{\beta l}(1+l/(\lambda h))^2
  3522	    =h^{\beta l}+\frac{2l}{\lambda}h^{\beta l-1}
  3523	    +\frac{l^2}{\lambda^2}h^{\beta l-2}.
  3524	  \]
  3525	  Since $\beta > 2$ and $l \ge 2$, all three powers are positive. The singleton
  3526	  mean likewise has powers $\beta,\beta-1$, and the cross singleton has power $p
  3527	  = 2-\alpha_0 > 0$. Thus, each whole local weight increases with $h$; we do not
  3528	  bound the inverse-length factor separately. At $h = LT/i$, $1+l/(\lambda h) =
  3529	  1+li/(kL) \le 1+li/k$, since $L \ge 1$. The remaining powers of $L$ are
  3530	  absorbed in the allowed $C^k$. For a singleton let $m_i,c_i$ be the first and
  3531	  second table weights. Every one of its splits is bounded by $m_i+c_i$. The
  3532	  higher-degree table weight is already uniform over its splits. Hence, the
  3533	  previously counted $\prod_i(2k_i+1) \le 3^k$ bounds all split choices once,
  3534	  using these combined singleton weights; that is the factor absorbed into $C^k$
  3535	  above. Substituting $h_i \le LT/i$ and $\lambda = k/T$ therefore extracts
  3536	  $C^kR_\alpha^kT^{\beta k}$, leaving $v_i$ at $k_i = 1$ and $b_{i,l}$ at $k_i =
  3537	  l \ge 2$ from Lemma~\ref{L:inventory-product}.
  3538	
  3539	  There is no further multinomial factor: for nonnegative weights $w_{i,0} = 1$,
  3540	  ordinary multiplication of power series gives exactly
  3541	  \[
  3542	    \sum_{\sum_i k_i=k}\prod_i w_{i,k_i}
  3543	    =[z^k]\prod_i\left(\sum_{l\ge0}w_{i,l}z^l\right).
  3544	  \]
  3545	  Apply this identity to the sum in~\eqref{E:interval-energy-splits}, using the
  3546	  two singleton alternatives together in $v_i$. Lemma~\ref{L:inventory-product}
  3547	  now proves \eqref{E:interval-coefficient-bound} at the finite cutoffs.
  3548	
  3549	  \emph{Identification and summation.} Keep positive smoothing, finite interval
  3550	  family and a fixed coefficient. The finite-degree multiplication bound used
  3551	  in~\eqref{E:interval-entire-majorant} is uniform in mode and band cutoffs. On
  3552	  finite-coordinate Gaussian vectors the omitted annihilation tail is zero and
  3553	  the creation tail tends to zero by its omitted pointwise variances and
  3554	  dominated convergence. Density in each finite degree extends this strong
  3555	  convergence. Closedness identifies the limit with multiplication by the
  3556	  measurable smoothed field. Fourier projections converge strongly and commute
  3557	  with free evolution. Dominated time integration thus identifies every fixed
  3558	  Duhamel word. The selected coefficients of the local Hermite truncation were
  3559	  already equal to those untruncated words. The full series is constructed
  3560	  separately using~\eqref{E:interval-entire-majorant}, choosing a sufficient
  3561	  degree cutoff anew at each order. A fixed-degree truncated propagator is not
  3562	  identified with the full evolution. The entire majorant gives convergence
  3563	  uniformly on compact amplitude sets. The coefficients estimated above are
  3564	  therefore those of the finite-interval model, with no zero-smoothing limit at
  3565	  this step.
  3566	
  3567	  The nonuniform number $v_{\max}$ was used only for this identification. The
  3568	  uniform coefficient bound contains no such number. Its constants come from
  3569	  $\delta_{\alpha/2}$, the fixed phase bound, the interval-length bound lemma
  3570	  and $L,c$; covariance enters only through $R_\alpha^k$. The zero-order energy
  3571	  is at most $e\|v\|_{1/T}^2$. Put $x = CR_\alpha T^\beta$ and $Y = e^{\nu
  3572	  x^{1/\nu}} \ge 1$. Since $\nu > 1$, $\sum_{k\ge0}x^k/(k!)^\nu \le Y$. Summing
  3573	  the coefficient bounds in absolute value gives
  3574	  \[
  3575	    \E\|\mathcal{U}(T;1)v\|_{1/T}^2
  3576	    \le(e+Y-1)\|v\|_{1/T}^2\le eY\|v\|_{1/T}^2.
  3577	  \]
  3578	  Absorbing $\nu C^{1/\nu}$ into the parameter-only constant proves
  3579	  \eqref{E:interval-phase-bound}. This proves
  3580	  Proposition~\ref{P:interval-coefficients}.
  3581	\end{proof}

    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
